name: Luxembourg — Luxembourgish parties
intro: compare it with Luxembourgish political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Luxembourg: those represented in the parliament (Chambre des Députés) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Chambre des Députés) after the 2023 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 60 members.

Lénk.name: déi Lénk
Lénk.priorities: Affordable housing, Taxing wealth, Public services
Lénk.description: The Left, a democratic-socialist party focused on housing and taxing wealth.

Gréng.name: déi gréng
Gréng.priorities: Climate action, Affordable housing, Public services
Gréng.description: The Greens, in government from 2013 to 2023.

LSAP.name: Lëtzebuerger Sozialistesch Aarbechterpartei
LSAP.priorities: Affordable housing, Workers' rights and wages, Welfare state
LSAP.description: Socialist Workers' Party, the main centre-left party, in opposition since 2023.

Piraten.name: Piratepartei Lëtzebuerg
Piraten.priorities: Transparency and digital rights, Digital innovation, Animal welfare
Piraten.description: Pirate Party, focused on transparency, digital rights and animal welfare.

Volt.name: Volt Luxembourg
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

DP.name: Demokratesch Partei
DP.priorities: Competitiveness and growth, Education, Civil liberties
DP.description: Democratic Party of former prime minister Xavier Bettel, liberal and in government with the CSV.

CSV.name: Chrëschtlech-Sozial Vollekspartei
CSV.priorities: Affordable housing, Fiscal discipline, Security and law and order
CSV.description: Christian Social People's Party of Prime Minister Luc Frieden, the largest party in Luxembourg.

ADR.name: Alternativ Demokratesch Reformpartei
ADR.priorities: National language and culture, National identity, Pensions and the elderly
ADR.description: Alternative Democratic Reform Party, national-conservative and focused on the Luxembourgish language.
